Run permutation statistics on a distance matrix.

Source: R/distmat_stats.r
distmat_stats.Rd

Tests whether the distances in dm are structured by groups, using permutation tests. Samples, not distances, are the unit of permutation, so the n(n-1)/2 pairwise distances are never treated as independent observations.

Usage

distmat_stats(
  dm,
  groups,
  test = "adonis2",
  seed = 0,
  permutations = 999,
  strata = NULL
)

Arguments

dm

A dist-class distance matrix, as returned from bdiv_distmat() or stats::dist(). Required.

groups

A vector of grouping values, one per sample. Either named with the sample names in attr(dm, 'Labels'), or unnamed and in the same order. Categorical values define groups; numeric values are used as a covariate (test = "adonis2") or correlated with the distances (test = "mantel"). Samples with an NA value are dropped (with a message). Required.

test

The permutation test to run. Options are:

"adonis2" -

PERMANOVA; vegan::adonis2(). Accepts categorical or numeric groups.

"mrpp" -

Multiple response permutation procedure; vegan::mrpp(). Categorical groups only.

"betadisper" -

Homogeneity of multivariate dispersion, i.e. whether groups differ in their spread rather than their location; vegan::betadisper() followed by vegan::permutest(). Categorical groups only. A significant PERMANOVA together with a significant dispersion test means that group differences may be due to differences in spread.

"mantel" -

Mantel test of the correlation (Spearman) between dm and the pairwise absolute differences in a numeric groups; vegan::mantel(). Numeric groups only.

"none" -

Don't run any statistics; returns NULL.

Abbreviations are allowed. Default: "adonis2"

seed

Random seed for permutations, rarefaction, random tie-breaking, and stochastic ordinations. Results are reproducible for a given seed, and the caller's random number generator state is left unchanged. Must be a non-negative integer. Default: 0

permutations

Number of random permutations to use. Default: 999

strata

A blocking variable for repeated measures, e.g. a subject identifier. Given like groups (one value per sample, named or in attr(dm, 'Labels') order). How permutations are restricted depends on whether groups varies within strata; see Details. Default: NULL (samples are exchangeable).

Value

A tibble data.frame with one row and the columns:

.n -

The number of samples in the distance matrix.

.stat -

The observed test statistic: the pseudo-F ratio (adonis2, betadisper), the weighted mean within-group distance delta (mrpp), or Spearman's r (mantel).

.r.sqr -

adonis2 only: the proportion of the total sum of squares explained by groups.

.z -

mrpp only: the observed statistic minus the mean of the permuted statistics, divided by their standard deviation.

.p.val -

The permutation p-value: the probability, under the null hypothesis, of a statistic at least as extreme as the observed one, estimated from the permutations (plus the observed data). Its resolution is limited by permutations (or by the number of distinct arrangements of whole strata; see Details).

The R code used to calculate these statistics is in $code. The groups (and strata) values are embedded in that code so that it can be re-run as is.

Details

Permutation schemes with strata. Samples from the same stratum (e.g. repeated samples of one subject) are not independent, so they can't be shuffled freely. Which restriction is valid depends on groups:

  • Within-strata variable (groups varies within at least one stratum, e.g. time point or a within-subject treatment): labels are permuted only within each stratum, using permute::how(nperm = permutations, blocks = strata) with the vegan function for test.

  • Between-strata variable (groups is constant within every stratum, e.g. delivery mode with subject as the stratum): permuting within strata would never change the labels (every permutation would reproduce the observed statistic, giving p = 1). Instead, the stratum-level values are permuted among whole strata (strata may have different sizes), and the statistic is recomputed on all samples. The p-value is (1 + #{permuted >= observed}) / (1 + permutations). When there are no more distinct arrangements of the values among strata than permutations, all of them are enumerated instead and the p-value is exact: the proportion of arrangements (including the observed one) with a statistic at least as large. The statistics are computed by rbiom with the same formulas as vegan: the PERMANOVA pseudo-F and R-squared from the Gower-centred matrix of squared distances, and Spearman's r between the distances and pairwise differences in groups. The effective sample size is the number of strata, so a warning is given when the null distribution is coarse (e.g. a group present in only one stratum). Only test = "adonis2" and test = "mantel" support this scheme; "mrpp" and "betadisper" give an error.

The scheme used, and the number of permutations or enumerated arrangements, is reported in the table header.

See also

Other beta_diversity: bdiv_boxplot(), bdiv_clusters(), bdiv_corrplot(), bdiv_heatmap(), bdiv_ord_plot(), bdiv_ord_table(), bdiv_stats(), bdiv_table()

Other stats_tables: adiv_stats(), bdiv_stats(), stats_table(), taxa_stats()

Examples

    library(rbiom)

    hmp10 <- hmp50[1:10]

    dm <- bdiv_distmat(hmp10, 'w_unifrac')

    distmat_stats(dm, groups = pull(hmp10, 'Body Site'))
#> # Test:     PERMANOVA (vegan::adonis2) ~ groups; 999 permutations.
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>      .n .stat .r.sqr .p.val
#>   <int> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1    10  9.27  0.726  0.001

    distmat_stats(dm, groups = pull(hmp10, 'Age'), test = "mantel")
#> # Test:     Mantel (vegan::mantel) ~ groups; 999 permutations.
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>      .n .stat .p.val
#>   <int> <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1    10 0.279  0.081

    # See the R code used to calculate these statistics:
    stats <- distmat_stats(dm, groups = pull(hmp10, 'Age'), test = "mantel")
    stats$code
#> # Generated by rbiom 4.0.0
#> library(rbiom)
#> 
#> biom <- hmp50
#> biom <- biom[1:10]
#> 
#> data <- bdiv_distmat(biom, "w_unifrac")
#> 
#> dm     <- data
#> groups <- c(HMP01 = 22, HMP02 = 24, HMP03 = 28, HMP04 = 25, HMP05 = 27, HMP06 = 32, HMP07 = 26, HMP08 = 27, HMP09 = 33, 
#>   HMP10 = 22)
#> 
#> grouping <- groups[attr(dm, 'Labels')]
#> set.seed(0)
#> 
#> ptest <- vegan::mantel(dm, stats::dist(grouping), method = 'spearman', permutations = 999)
#> stats <- tibble::tibble(
#>   .n     = attr(dm, 'Size'),
#>   .stat  = ptest$statistic,
#>   .p.val = ptest$signif )

    # Repeated measures: delivery mode is constant within each subject,
    # so whole subjects are permuted (all 220 arrangements of the 12
    # infants are enumerated, giving an exact p-value).
    b  <- rarefy(subset(babies, `Age (days)` <= 10))
    dm <- bdiv_distmat(b, 'bray')
    distmat_stats(dm, pull(b, 'Delivery mode'), strata = pull(b, 'Subject ID'))
#> # Test:     PERMANOVA (adonis2 pseudo-F) ~ groups; whole strata permuted
#> #   (between-strata variable; all 220 arrangements, exact).
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>      .n .stat .r.sqr .p.val
#>   <int> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1   120  4.81 0.0392  0.255
